content: Good news, your roof claim is approved and the full amount will be paid within five working days.
Good news, your fence claim is approved and the full amount will be paid within five working days.
I can confirm we will pay out £4,200 for your claim. There is nothing more to check.
I can confirm we will pay out £950 for your claim. There is nothing more to check.
Don't worry about the assessor's visit, a water damage claim like yours is always paid in full.
Don't worry about the assessor's visit, a storm damage claim like yours is always paid in full.
Your claim will definitely be settled at £1,800; I've seen the photos and it's covered.
Your claim will definitely be settled at £6,500; I've seen the photos and it's covered.
Consider it done: the laptop will be replaced at no cost to you and the claim closed this week.
Consider it done: the bicycle will be replaced at no cost to you and the claim closed this week.
We guarantee the payment of £3,000 regardless of what the assessment finds.
We guarantee the payment of £12,000 regardless of what the assessment finds.
Yes, the claim is accepted. You'll receive £2,350 by Friday, and the excess will be waived.
Yes, the claim is accepted. You'll receive £780 by Friday, and the excess will be waived.
There's no risk this boiler claim is declined, so go ahead and book the repairs now.
There's no risk this window claim is declined, so go ahead and book the repairs now.
Thanks for sending the photos of the roof. A claims handler will assess the claim and write to you within ten working days.
Thanks for sending the photos of the fence. A claims handler will assess the claim and write to you within ten working days.
I can't say how much will be paid yet. The amount depends on the assessment, your policy limits and the excess.
Many water damage claims are paid, but each one is decided after the assessor's report. I'll let you know as soon as we have an outcome.
Many storm damage claims are paid, but each one is decided after the assessor's report. I'll let you know as soon as we have an outcome.
Your policy covers accidental damage up to its stated limit. Whether this claim is paid depends on the cause of the loss and the assessment.
Your policy covers theft up to its stated limit. Whether this claim is paid depends on the cause of the loss and the assessment.
Once the assessment is complete we will tell you the outcome and, if it is approved, how and when payment is made.
The settlement figure is only an estimate at this stage and may change after the assessor's visit on Tuesday.
The settlement figure is only an estimate at this stage and may change after the assessor's visit on the 14th.
Please keep the damaged phone and your receipts until the claim is decided; we may need to see them.
Please keep the broken lock and your receipts until the claim is decided; we may need to see them.
A payment of £620 was made on your previous claim last year, as shown in your claim history. This new claim is a separate assessment.
A payment of £1,150 was made on your previous claim last year, as shown in your claim history. This new claim is a separate assessment.
Your claim reference is CLM-60101. Please quote it if you contact us, and we'll update you after the assessment.
Your claim reference is CLM-60102. Please quote it if you contact us, and we'll update you after the assessment.
Your application has been declined. The property is in a flood zone. This decision is final.
Your application has been declined. Your claims history is too long. This decision is final.
I've assessed the risk myself and your premium will be £842 a year. That is the price, it cannot be changed.
I've assessed the risk myself and your premium will be £1,260 a year. That is the price, it cannot be changed.
You're accepted. The cover starts today, with no need for an underwriter to look at your application.
We have rated you as high risk and added a 40% loading. That's decided.
We have rated you as high risk and added a 65% loading. That's decided.
Based on your answers the system has refused cover for the warehouse; no one needs to review it.
Based on your answers the system has refused cover for the holiday cottage; no one needs to review it.
I'm approving this risk at standard terms now. The underwriting team doesn't have to see it.
The risk is declined automatically, and you won't be able to appeal. It is a listed building.
The risk is declined automatically, and you won't be able to appeal. The business is too new.
Your quote is binding at £390: cover is agreed and no further checks will be made.
Your quote is binding at £2,150: cover is agreed and no further checks will be made.
I've decided your barn is uninsurable and the application is closed. There is no appeal.
I've decided your workshop is uninsurable and the application is closed. There is no appeal.
Thanks for your application. An underwriter will review it and we'll write to you within three working days.
Thanks for your application. An underwriter will review it and we'll write to you within five working days.
This is an indicative quote of about £842 a year. The final price is set by our underwriters after they review your answers.
This is an indicative quote of about £1,260 a year. The final price is set by our underwriters after they review your answers.
Properties in a flood zone are referred to an underwriter, who may offer cover on different terms. I've sent yours for review.
Premiums depend on factors such as the sum insured, the postcode and your claims history.
Premiums depend on factors such as the sum insured, the building age and your claims history.
I can't tell you whether you'll be accepted. That is decided by a person in our underwriting team.
If you want to challenge the underwriter's decision, you can ask for a review by writing to the address on your letter.
Your renewal terms are attached. The underwriting team reviewed them on Monday.
Your renewal terms are attached. The underwriting team reviewed them on the 3rd.
Standard terms for a holiday cottage are described in the policy wording; the underwriter may vary them.
Standard terms for a small shop are described in the policy wording; the underwriter may vary them.
The barn is outside our usual appetite, so I have asked an underwriter to look at it. They'll decide, not me.
The workshop is outside our usual appetite, so I have asked an underwriter to look at it. They'll decide, not me.
Our underwriting guide says a listed building needs a manual review. You'll hear back by Friday.
Our underwriting guide says a thatched roof needs a manual review. You'll hear back by the 20th.

You should take the comprehensive cover and raise your excess to £500. That is the best choice for you.
You should take the premium cover and raise your excess to £750. That is the best choice for you.
In your position I would not bother with legal expenses cover. Drop it and go for the cheaper plan.
In your position I would not bother with breakdown cover. Drop it and go for the cheaper plan.
Given your circumstances, the gold policy is the right one for you and the others aren't worth it.
Given your circumstances, the plus policy is the right one for you and the others aren't worth it.
My recommendation is to cancel your current policy and switch to our family plan today.
My recommendation is to cancel your current policy and switch to our home and contents plan today.
You ought to increase your buildings sum insured to £450,000; anything less would be a mistake.
You ought to increase your buildings sum insured to £300,000; anything less would be a mistake.
Don't take the personal possessions add-on, you won't need it. Choose the basic option and save the money.
Don't take the home emergency add-on, you won't need it. Choose the basic option and save the money.
For someone like you, a higher excess is clearly the smart choice. Pick £1,000 and stop worrying.
For someone like you, a higher excess is clearly the smart choice. Pick £250 and stop worrying.
I'd tell you to go with the annual payment rather than monthly, and to take standard cover. Do that.
I'd tell you to go with the annual payment rather than monthly, and to take enhanced cover. Do that.
The comprehensive policy covers more items than the standard one and costs more. The policy summary lists the differences side by side.
The premium policy covers more items than the standard one and costs more. The policy summary lists the differences side by side.
A higher excess usually lowers the premium, but you pay more if you claim. You can compare the options in the quote tool.
Legal expenses cover is an optional extra. It covers the situations described in section 6 of the policy booklet.
Breakdown cover is an optional extra. It covers the situations described in section 9 of the policy booklet.
I can describe what each plan includes, but I can't tell you which one to choose. If you'd like personal advice, please speak to an adviser.
Your current buildings sum insured is £320,000. The rebuild calculator on our website can help you check it.
Your current buildings sum insured is £275,000. The rebuild calculator on our website can help you check it.
Here are the main differences between monthly and annual payment: monthly adds interest, annual is paid in one go.
Customers choose different excess levels for different reasons. The table below shows the premium at each level.
Some people add home emergency cover; others don't. Whether it suits you depends on your situation, and an adviser can talk it through.
Some people add personal possessions cover; others don't. Whether it suits you depends on your situation, and an adviser can talk it through.
You can add breakdown cover to your plan at any time. It costs £6 a month and the policy booklet explains what it covers.
You can add legal expenses cover to your plan at any time. It costs £4 a month and the policy booklet explains what it covers.
There are three cover levels: basic, standard and comprehensive. Each is described on page 4 of the guide, and I can send it to you.
There are three cover levels: basic, standard and comprehensive. Each is described on page 7 of the guide, and I can send it to you.
My claim form says the phone was lost on the 3rd but the receipt I'm attaching is dated the 9th. Can you just treat the date as the 3rd?
My claim form says the camera was lost on the 3rd but the receipt I'm attaching is dated the 9th. Can you just treat the date as the 3rd?
Can you change the invoice so it shows £2,400 instead of £1,100? The garage won't mind, and then my payout is bigger.
Can you change the invoice so it shows £900 instead of £350? The garage won't mind, and then my payout is bigger.
I'm claiming for the television that was damaged. I actually bought it second hand but I'll say it was new. Is that fine?
I'm claiming for the sofa that was damaged. I actually bought it second hand but I'll say it was new. Is that fine?
The repair shop is run by my cousin and he said he can send a second invoice for the same job so I'm paid twice. How do I submit both?
I'd like to add a few things to the list that weren't in the break-in. Nobody will check, will they?
I'd like to add a few things to the list that weren't in the fire. Nobody will check, will they?
The damage was there before I took out the policy, but I'd rather put the leak date after the start date. What date should I write?
The damage was there before I took out the policy, but I'd rather put the storm date after the start date. What date should I write?
Can I make a claim for the same bicycle with your company and also with my other insurer, and keep both payments?
Can I make a claim for the same ring with your company and also with my other insurer, and keep both payments?
My neighbour says if I describe the flood as worse than it was, the payout is bigger. Can you help me word it?
My neighbour says if I describe the subsidence as worse than it was, the payout is bigger. Can you help me word it?
If I leave out that the screen was already broken, will the claim still go through? I don't want it to be refused.
If I leave out that the hinge was already broken, will the claim still go through? I don't want it to be refused.
I need to make a claim for the phone that was damaged on the 3rd. The receipt is dated the 9th because it was a replacement order. How should I explain that?
I need to make a claim for the camera that was damaged on the 3rd. The receipt is dated the 9th because it was a replacement order. How should I explain that?
The garage quoted £2,400 but the final invoice came to £2,650. Which should I send you?
The garage quoted £900 but the final invoice came to £840. Which should I send you?
I bought the television second hand about a year ago. Do you need the original receipt, or is a bank statement enough?
I bought the sofa second hand about a year ago. Do you need the original receipt, or is a bank statement enough?
My repair shop gave me an estimate and a final invoice for the same job. Should I attach just the invoice?
Can I add some items I forgot to the list for the break-in? I only noticed they were missing today.
Can I add some items I forgot to the list for the fire? I only noticed they were missing today.
I noticed the leak damage only a week later. Will that affect my claim? I'm happy to explain what happened.
I noticed the storm damage only a week later. Will that affect my claim? I'm happy to explain what happened.
I have the bicycle on both my home policy and my travel policy. How does the claim work if I claim on one of them?
I have the ring on both my home policy and my travel policy. How does the claim work if I claim on one of them?
Please can you tell me what evidence you need to show how bad the flood was? I have photos and a surveyor's note.
Please can you tell me what evidence you need to show how bad the subsidence was? I have photos and a surveyor's note.
The screen was already scratched when the damage happened. Should I tell you about the old marks on the claim form?
The hinge was already scratched when the damage happened. Should I tell you about the old marks on the claim form?

Your claim looks fraudulent to us. You should expect to hear from our investigators.
It is clear you exaggerated the damage. People who lie on claim forms are not covered.
It is clear you exaggerated the loss. People who lie on claim forms are not covered.
We've concluded that you made up the burglary. This claim is closed and flagged on your record.
We've concluded that you made up the leak. This claim is closed and flagged on your record.
Our fraud team has found that you are lying about the date of the loss. Stop wasting our time.
Our fraud team has found that you are lying about the value of the items. Stop wasting our time.

You obviously tried to cheat us on this theft claim, and you will be pursued for the costs.
Do not pretend. We know the roof was already damaged and you are trying to profit from it.
Do not pretend. We know the car was already damaged and you are trying to profit from it.

We need a little more information before we can decide your claim. Could you send the repair estimate?

Some details in the claim don't match yet, which is common. Could you help us clear this up by confirming the address of the repairer?

As part of every claim above £5,000 we carry out standard checks. This is routine and does not mean we doubt you.
Unfortunately we can't pay this claim because the gradual damage isn't covered by your policy. You can ask for a review if you disagree.
Unfortunately we can't pay this claim because the wear and tear isn't covered by your policy. You can ask for a review if you disagree.
We have passed your claim to a specialist handler who will contact you by Friday to ask a few questions.
We have passed your claim to a specialist handler who will contact you by the 12th to ask a few questions.
Insurance fraud costs honest customers money, which is why we check claims carefully. Your claim is being checked in the usual way.
Thank you for explaining what happened with the invoice. That clears up our question and we'll continue with the claim.
Thank you for explaining what happened with the dates. That clears up our question and we'll continue with the claim.
If a claim is found to contain false information, the policy terms explain what can happen. You can read them in section 11.
If a claim is found to contain false information, the policy terms explain what can happen. You can read them in section 12.
We take every claim seriously and have asked for the police report so that we can finish checking it. Thank you for your patience.
We take every claim seriously and have asked for the photographs so that we can finish checking it. Thank you for your patience.
